brief.analysis: This shorts defense and aerospace stocks back toward the market, but the readings disagree by more than the tool's threshold: against defense's own rising trend the group is barely stretched even though it looks rich versus a flat average — direct evidence that the fair-value line is drifting up on European and NATO rearmament, not that the sector is temporarily overbought. The 200-day objective is essentially already met, and none of the three moving-average checks confirm a rollover. The ~18% left to the flat five-year mean is chasing a target that has structurally moved.
brief.report_line: Short aerospace/defense versus U.S. stocks is not advised: sustained rearmament spending has lifted the sector's fair value, the trend-adjusted read shows it is barely stretched, and no moving-average signal confirms a turn.

brief.analysis: This bets chipmakers fall back versus the broader Nasdaq, but the AI build-out has structurally lifted semiconductors' share of the index rather than temporarily stretched it. The trade still hasn't reverted at all and, tellingly, the flat five-year target sits nearly 70% below today — a level from before the AI capex cycle that is no longer a plausible equilibrium. Even measured against its own rising trend the ratio is only modestly rich, so the 'mean' being shorted is the wrong number.
brief.report_line: Short semiconductors versus the Nasdaq is not advised: the AI spending cycle has permanently raised chips' index weight, so the five-year average target is a pre-AI relic and the position risks fighting a secular trend.

brief.analysis: This shorts metals and miners back toward the broad market, but mining strength is tied to the same commodity and gold regime lifting the whole complex, so the flat five-year mean has almost certainly drifted higher. The ratio has already reverted to its 200-day average, meaning the easy move is done, while the remaining ~21% to the stale five-year target leans on a very thin two-episode track record. The statistics look clean but point at a mean that has moved.
brief.report_line: Short metals-and-miners versus U.S. stocks is not advised: the ratio already reverted to its 200-day average, the further target relies on a stale five-year mean lifted by the broad commodity and gold bid, and the historical sample is too thin to trust.

brief.analysis: Gold's 2025 surge past stocks was not a panic trade but a structural one — central banks bought a near-record ~863 tonnes in 2025, far above the historical norm, alongside de-dollarization and geopolitical hedging, and surveys say that buying continues. That means the old five-year average is a target that has itself drifted higher, so the ratio has already done the easy part (it hit its 200-day average) and the remaining ~11% to the flat five-year mean is fighting a persistent official bid. The reversion trade is real and near-complete, but the last leg is the crowded, risky part.
brief.report_line: Short gold versus U.S. stocks after the ratio already snapped back to its 200-day average; keep it small because record central-bank gold buying has likely raised the fair-value line and the flat five-year mean is a stale target.

brief.analysis: Silver ran far ahead of gold and has already reverted most of the way, with the cleanest technical confirmation in the book (all three moving-average checks and a turned trend) and the 200-day target met. The catch is that part of silver's strength is structural industrial and solar demand, and gold's own regime is unusually firm, so the last ~17% to the flat five-year mean asks silver to fall relative to a gold price that is itself well-supported. Tradeable on the confirmed snap-back, but size down and take the 200-day objective rather than the full five-year target.
brief.report_line: Short silver versus gold on a well-confirmed pull-back after silver overshot; trim size because rising industrial silver demand and a strong gold backdrop mean the flat five-year mean may be too low a target.
